newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill two police, free prisoner in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill two police, free prisoner in Pakistan.

text.p: Gunmen killed two policemen and wounded two others and a patient at a hospital in Karachi on Monday before escaping with a prisoner under treatment, police said.
At least three gunmen were involved in the early morning attack on the government's civil hospital in a busy district of the city.
Police identified the escaped prisoner as Asghar Shah, an activist of the Sindhi nationalist Jiye Sindh party who was serving a 25-year jail term.
Separately, police said the bullet-riddled body of a 30-year-old activist of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) had been found in a sack in another part of the city on Sunday.
No group has claimed responsibility for the death of the MQM party worker, whose body bore marks of torture.
Violence between the MQM and a splinter MQM-Haqiqi faction has risen since national and provincial elections on February 3.

After the polls, the MQM, led by London-based Altaf Hussain, joined with Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League to form a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital.
Over 800 people were killed in ethnic, political and sectarian strife in the southern port city last year following more than 2,000 in 1995.
